editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article text, reviews and lyrics are never copied or reproduced; facts are stated in Swoon'd's own words with links to the original source.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: She can follow a conversation about a song, an album or a show, hear a beat, a build and the major-or-minor colour for herself, ask a couple of genuinely curious questions about a favourite artist, and say 'okay, I see why this matters to you' without faking it.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Only original synthesised or produced audio (licence original-swoond) or audio under an explicit registered licence; no commercial recordings, no snippets of hits, no clones of a specific work. Real songs are reached only through the streaming platform's official app or embed under its terms (spec sections 20 and 40).
Lyrics are never reproduced or ingested, including short quotes; example lines in lessons are invented.
Procedural or original illustrations only (license original-swoond); no album or cover art, artist photos or posters without a written licence.
Label, tour, festival, awards and platform (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Ticketmaster) marks: text mentions and link-outs only.
No embedded concert or music-video footage; deep-link to official channels.
Never copy publisher or review text; headlines with links only.

Provider APIs (Spotify, Apple, Ticketmaster, Bandsintown, Setlist.fm, Luminate) have restrictive terms; MusicBrainz core data is open but checked per dataset; every provider sits behind a Swoon'd adapter.
Artist names as facts only; no likeness, fabricated quotes or implied endorsement.

safetyConstraints: Hearing: loud music can cause cumulative hearing damage; teach music earplugs, distance from speakers and breaks; general information, not medical advice.
Crowds and festivals: note exits, water and meeting points; teach leaving unsafe crowds and de-escalation, never risk-taking; no content encouraging substance use or driving impaired.
Privacy and respect: never coach chasing artists, locating private addresses or approaching artists off-stage.
Scams: teach official resale channels and warn about too-good-to-be-true tickets.
Mental health: music tied to grief or hard times is handled warmly with no diagnosis or advice; point to real people.
Never encourage the learner to fake expertise or taste with the person they care about; never grade taste.
